author: Slidebean
description:
Humanoid robots don’t fail at tasks. They fail at presence.

The hardest part of building humanoid robots isn’t hardware.

It’s designing something humans feel comfortable interacting with.

Fauna’s approach flips the usual playbook, focusing less on strength and more on social awareness.

Their bet is simple:
People won’t pay for robots that work harder.
They’ll pay for robots that feel right.

title: The real test for humanoid robots isn’t performance.
